intro: Lesson 20: The heart and circulation. To understand how the heart pumps blood around a double circulation

picture.alt: A diagram of the four chambers of the heart
picture.draw: Draw and label: Heart diagram labelling sheet

questions.q: Describe the journey of blood from the body to the lungs.
questions.a: Body, vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs.
questions.model: Start where blood returns: from the body into the right atrium. Then into the right ventricle. The right ventricle pumps it to the lungs. So: body, right atrium, right ventricle, lungs.

questions.q: Why is the left ventricle wall thicker than the right?
questions.a: It pumps blood all around the body, which needs more pressure.

questions.q: Core: Label the heart diagram (four chambers, valves, vessels) and colour oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
questions.a: Left side red (oxygenated), right side blue (deoxygenated); chambers and valves labelled.
questions.model: Teacher labels the right atrium first and colours it blue: blood returning from the body has little oxygen.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why it is called a double circulation. Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Blood passes through the heart twice in one full circuit: once to the lungs and once to the body.

questions.q: Stretch: Fish have a single circulation. Suggest one disadvantage.
questions.a: Blood loses pressure in the gills, so it flows slowly to the body and delivers oxygen more slowly.

questions.q: The right side of the heart pumps blood to the...
Big question: why does blood go through the heart twice on each trip around the body?
questions.a: To get oxygen in the lungs and then be pumped at high pressure to the body.
